Build me a medieval rural hamlet on a broad, gently rolling grassy plain beneath a bright, softly clouded sky. Arrange roughly a dozen buildings in an irregular loose cluster around branching dirt lanes and several open grassy courtyards, leaving wide gaps between the outer structures and open countryside visible at every edge. Mix long one- and two-storey timber-framed houses with pale plaster infill, dark exposed beams, stone foundations, steep thatched roofs, small shuttered windows, and heavy wooden doors; add several plainer dark wooden barns with tall gabled roofs and a few large rectangular stone buildings capped by dark thatch. Place the largest half-timbered houses near the central junction, with barns and stone structures spread around the perimeter and facing inward toward paths or clearings. Include a few small thatched sheds between them, plus an open-sided thatched market or work shelter containing simple wooden equipment and a faint warm glow. Add short stone steps at raised doorways, occasional covered porches, multiple smoking chimneys, worn earth around entrances, and long directional shadows. Keep the settlement organic, quiet, minimally furnished, and moderately spaced rather than crowded.
